Maya: Quick Q — for design partner contracts, do we want to bake in 'priority tunneling' so DP traffic gets routing priority over general beta? Thinking SLA buckets: Critical (p99 < 200ms), Standard (p95 < 500ms). Thoughts? :thinking_face:
Sam: I like the idea but worried about cost. We should define clear criteria for when DP gets tunnelized (active experiment, urgent bugfix, demo windows).
Priya: Agree. Suggest a 3‑tier contract: 1) Launch-window priority (2 weeks), 2) Canary priority (rolling 10% traffic for 7 days), 3) Escalation priority (on-call intervention). Each tier needs explicit capacity + cost offset.
Jin: If we codify this, ops needs a concrete routing policy example. For example: `route_policy: { priority_group: "dp", max_qps: 50, fallback_model: "small-quant" }`
Katie: Also include churn/dropout mitigation — opt-in cadence, trial credits, and a clear rollback SLA for any changes that break the partner flow.
Maya: Proposed next steps: draft contract language for the three tiers + sample routing config + cost impact estimate. Who can own which piece?
Sam: I can draft routing config and run a quick cost delta (GPU hours, burst pricing) by EOD Friday.
Priya: I'll sketch the contract language and define success criteria (engagement, retention, bug counts, NPS).
Jin: I'll produce a short ops CLI snippet and a smoke test harness. Example test command: 
```
redwood route apply --policy dp-priority --max-qps 50 --fallback model-small-quant
redwood test smoke --policy dp-priority --samples 200
```
Katie: +1. Also will schedule 30m with Legal to sign off on liability/data retention clauses and any SLAs tied to uptime.
DeployBot: [deployment] Canary policy `dp-priority` applied to cluster-5 at 50 qps — monitoring hooks enabled.
Maya: Fantastic. Once drafts are in, we'll run a dry-run with one active partner next week. Ping me when you're done. :raised_hands:
